newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HEDGING SAVES ANGLO FROM WORST OF GOLD FALL.
newsitem.headline: HEDGING SAVES ANGLO FROM WORST OF GOLD FALL.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday that an active hedging strategy had saved it from even heavier losses in the March quarter following a sharp fall in the bullion price.
The mining house's long-term, regularly reviewed hedging strategy won for it a gold price five percent higher than the average spot price in the three months to end-March.

Anglo gold mines achieved 53,308 rand in average gold revenue per kg sold -- a four percent decline on the preceding quarter's price but not as much as the almost 11 percent shrinking in the spot bullion price during the period.

"Due to our active hedging programme the decrease in the price received by the companies which report today has been limited to four percent which, incidentally, I think is quite a good achievement and shows in rather concrete terms the value of having an active hedging activity," said Bobby Godsell, chief executive of Anglo's gold mines.
Anglo said on Thursday its gold mines recorded available profit of 224.3 million rand in the quarter to end-March, 34 percent down on the previous quarter.
Anglo marketing manager Kelvin Williams said that the group's hedging strategy would be able to maintain similar gold revenues for some time yet.
"I think you can assume that we will be able to maintain these sorts of prices in the future for some time. Our prices are in the vicinity of 53,000 rand a kg," Williams said.
"This is obviously a consequence of a stabilisation enhancement that does come from a practice of ongoing managed hedging rather than one-off hedging," he added.
Williams said that Anglo's total amount of hedge had been drawn down to around 168 tonnes today.
But he emphasised that the figure was not absolute because the hedge was live and constantly being topped up or drawn down.
